title: Base Labs launches an open-weight AI safety partnership with Hugging Face and Goodfire
content:
Baseten launched a new safety infrastructure standard alongside its Base Labs research arm on Wednesday, partnering with Hugging Face and Goodfire AI to build safety evaluation and monitoring infrastructure for open-weight models.
The announcement lands amid debate for the safety of open-weight models — which can be made dangerous by removing their safeguards through a rising technique known as abliteration. The scale of the problem is massive: Hugging Face, which hosts open-source AI models, currently lists over 6,000 abliterated models.
Base Labs, the research group Baseten spun up earlier this year, will develop and publish methods for training and monitoring open models. The company is framing their future work as a “standard” for open models that is transparent and built into how models are trained and deployed, rather than bolted on afterward.
“We believe openness to be an advantage for AI safety,” the company said on X. “Openness provides more visibility into the behavior of models and, most importantly, greater means of turning safety research into actionable and transparent controls than closed-source.”
The companies haven’t disclosed how the partnership will work technically, though Goodfire framed the goal in a reply to Baseten’s post: “Safety must be built into open models and provided by those who serve them.” Goodfire, which specializes in opening AI’s “black box” to explain how models make decisions, is the likeliest candidate for the “built into” part.
Baseten, an AI inference provider, raised a $1.5 billion Series F in June, vaulting its valuation to $13 billion. Partner Goodfire AI is similarly well-capitalized, having raised a $150 million Series B led by B Capital earlier this year to advance its model interpretability platform.
Looking ahead, Baseten is putting out an open call to the broader developer ecosystem to contribute to the framework. “Together, we are building an ecosystem of open models that are safe and accessible to all,” the company noted.

report.summary: Baseten's Base Labs partners with Hugging Face and Goodfire to build open-weight AI safety evaluation and monitoring infrastructure as abliterated models proliferate.
report.background: Open-weight AI models offer transparency and accessibility, but their safeguards can be stripped using abliteration, a technique that removes refusal behavior. Hugging Face currently hosts over 6,000 abliterated models, highlighting the scale of the problem. Baseten, an inference provider valued at $13 billion after a $1.5 billion Series F, spun up Base Labs earlier this year. Partner Goodfire AI, which raised a $150 million Series B, focuses on model interpretability. The partnership aims to make safety a built-in standard for training and deployment rather than an afterthought. Technical details remain undisclosed, but Baseten is inviting developers to contribute.
key_points: Base Labs, Baseten's research arm, launched a partnership with Hugging Face and Goodfire AI to create safety evaluation and monitoring infrastructure for open-weight models. The group argues openness improves AI safety by giving researchers more visibility into model behavior and more ways to turn safety research into transparent controls.

Abliteration, a rising technique for removing model safeguards, has produced over 6,000 abliterated models on Hugging Face. That figure illustrates the practical challenge: open-weight releases can be modified quickly, and safety measures added before release may not survive downstream changes.

Goodfire AI is the likely technical partner for embedding safety into models. It specializes in interpretability, or opening AI's black box to explain decisions. Goodfire said safety must be built into open models and provided by those who serve them.

The companies have not disclosed technical details. Baseten frames the effort as a transparent standard for training and deploying open models, not a bolt-on safety layer. It is also issuing an open call for the developer ecosystem to contribute to the framework.

Both partners are well capitalized. Baseten raised a $1.5 billion Series F in June at a $13 billion valuation. Goodfire raised a $150 million Series B led by B Capital. The funding signals serious commercial interest in open-model safety and interpretability.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the partnership could push open-weight safety from ad hoc patches toward shared standards and infrastructure, influencing how labs, cloud providers, and regulators assess model risk. For developers, it may yield new evaluation, monitoring, and interpretability tools, but also expectations around safe training and deployment. For regular users, safer open models could mean more trustworthy assistants and fewer harmful outputs, though abliterated variants will likely persist. The effort also tests whether openness can be framed as a safety advantage rather than a liability, a debate with major consequences for innovation, competition, and policy.
report.tools: Follow Hugging Face Hub for open models, datasets, and safety evaluations; Goodfire for interpretability tooling; and Baseten/Base Labs for inference and forthcoming safety methods. Developers can also explore open evaluation frameworks such as EleutherAI's lm-evaluation-harness, Stanford HELM, and MLCommons safety benchmarks to test model behavior.
